content: Finally, this measurement does not support our initial hypothesis that LGBTQ groups have been more negatively evaluated than the other social group American(s), but does reveal that the observed trend for LGBTQ labels is not merely an artifact of changing reporting styles, since paragraphs containing American(s) show a very different pattern. Overall, this result demonstrates substantial language change in the New York Times's discussion of LGBTQ people as well as variation in the contexts where different group labels appear, particularly homosexual.
